title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 292
paragraphs: Of the Egyptians themselves, those who dwell in the part of Egypt which is sown for crops practise memory more than any other men, and are by far the most learned in history of all those of whom I have had experience. Their manner of life is as follows. For three successive days in each month they purge, hunting after health with emetics and clysters, and they think that all the diseases that exist are produced in men by the food on which they live. For the Egyptians are from other causes also the most healthy of all men, next after the Libyans — in my opinion because of their seasons, for the seasons do not change; since diseases are most apt to be produced in men by the changes of things generally, and especially by the changes of the seasons. As for their diet: they eat bread, making loaves of emmer, which they call kyllestis; and they habitually use a wine made out of barley, for they have no vines in their land. Some of their fish they dry in the sun and then eat without cooking; others they eat cured in brine. Of birds, they eat quails, ducks, and small birds without cooking, after first curing them; and everything else of the class of birds or fishes that they have, except such as have been set apart as sacred, they eat roasted or boiled.
